s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss following traumatic injury to the head
salient_findings: Decreased vision in one eye after being struck by lightning
Central macular thickening on fundus examination at 2 weeks
Mild posterior subcapsular cataract visible in the affected eye at 7 weeks
key_facts: Patient is a white woman in her 20s
Unremarkable medical and ocular history
Symptoms began 4 days prior to presentation
Struck by lightning directly to the right forehead
Uncorrected visual acuity measured 20/50 OD and 20/20 OS
Pupils were symmetric, with no relative afferent pupillary defect
Initial anterior segment examination was normal
Initial dilated fundus examination showed no apparent abnormalities in either eye
Subtle irregularity of the outer retinal layers on initial OCT examination
Intraretinal cystoid changes and subfoveal ellipsoid zone disruption on OCT at 2 weeks
Restoration of foveal contour with decreased cystoid abnormalities on OCT at 7 weeks

shortlist.label: Commotio retinae
shortlist.why_kept: Subtle irregularity of the outer retinal layers and intraretinal cystoid changes following traumatic injury to the head

shortlist.label: Traumatic optic neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Decreased vision in one eye following direct trauma to the forehead

shortlist.label: Lightning-induced cataract
shortlist.why_kept: Development of posterior subcapsular cataract after being struck by lightning

shortlist.label: Traumatic cataract
shortlist.why_kept: Cataract formation after traumatic injury to the head

shortlist.label: Electrical injury to the eye
shortlist.why_kept: Ocular findings after direct lightning strike to the forehead

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms began after being struck by lightning, which is a form of electrical injury, and the subsequent development of cataract and retinal changes are consistent with electrical injury to the eye

rejected.label: Commotio retinae
rejected.why: While commotio retinae can cause retinal changes, it is typically associated with blunt trauma, not electrical injury

rejected.label: Traumatic optic neuropathy
rejected.why: There is no evidence of optic nerve damage or relative afferent pupillary defect

rejected.label: Lightning-induced cataract
rejected.why: While the patient did develop a cataract, the diagnosis of electrical injury to the eye encompasses a broader range of ocular injuries, including cataract

rejected.label: Traumatic cataract
rejected.why: The cataract is likely a result of the electrical injury, not just a traumatic cataract

rejected.label: Traumatic optic neuropathy
rejected.why: There is no evidence of optic nerve damage or relative afferent pupillary defect
